answer.rationale: Write-path p99 degradation began ~30 minutes after a release shipped 2 hours ago, making the release the leading suspect; memory_b1 documents a rollback clearing a similar post-release error spike without customer impact. Peak settlement traffic means I must sequence the rollback to drain or retry in-flight writes so none are lost. Other directions are weaker fits: failover and capacity address infrastructure/load, not a regression tied to a deploy; circuit breakers and read-replica routing target dependency or read load, not the write path. Rolling back is also reversible, preserving the option to add capacity next window if latency persists.
